move: gooey blob stretches into a bar, letters bud out, collapse back
how: An SVG on near-black with a yellow blob path and five yellow text letters (stroke same as fill) sharing a gooey filter (feGaussianBlur 10 plus alpha-boost colour matrix) so touching shapes fuse. The blob morphs with MorphSVG to a second wobbly shape over the first 22% (sine.inOut), then to a long horizontal bar by 47% (expo.inOut). From 40% the letters scale up from 0 to 1.15 with back.out(1.8) staggered from the centre while their stroke-width grows to 14, budding out of the bar; the bar flattens to scaleY .05 and the letters settle to scale 1 with stroke 4 by 82%. At 81% the letters collapse to scale 0 (stroke 20, power3.in, from the edges) as the bar re-inflates to full scale, and a set() at the very end snaps the path back to the original blob so the loop restarts on the shape.
adapt: Change the word (150px letter pitch from centre), the ink colour (fill and stroke together), the blob path pair and the caption. Keep the goo filter values and the blob-to-bar expo.inOut, which is what makes the letters read as emerging from the shape.
port: mount(el, shot) builds the SVG with a per-instance filter id, the blob path and one text element per letter with scale 0 set; animate(el, shot, D) returns a gsap.timeline with the morphs at 0 and 0.225D, letter pop 0.4D, bar flatten 0.475D, settle 0.65D, collapse 0.81D and the reset set() at D. Register MorphSVGPlugin; scope '#blob' to el.querySelector.
caveats: the return morph targets '#blob' (its own current data) so it is a no-op; the original shape is restored by a hard set() at the last frame, not tweened
letters do not morph from the shape, they pop out of the bar: an approximation of the description
goo filter on large glyphs is moderately slow
